clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1076 by source on develop: is the MULMOD memo active by default, where does it live, and can two workers or two frames share it.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched bor develop core/vm/mulmod_memo.go, evm.go and instructions.go. The memo is the field mulmodMemo of the EVM struct (evm.go line 219), and opMulmod always calls evm.mulmodMemo.mulmod (instructions.go line 202). The memo takes its path only when z[3] != 0, compares the whole uint256.Int value (mm.mod != *z, all four limbs, mulmod_memo.go line 57), stores a copy of the modulus and uint256.Reciprocal(z) before the in-place write, and then calls MulModWithReciprocal. bor develop go.mod pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. In that version MulModWithReciprocal (uint256.go lines 688-714) and MulMod (lines 720-746) run the same zero checks, the same umul, and the same reduce4 call when m[3] != 0, differing only in where mu comes from. Because the cached reciprocal is a pure function of the full modulus, a hit gives the same word as a recompute, so frame reverts, child frames and transactions sharing one EVM cannot see a stale value. FullMath.mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp therefore compute the same results under the memo.
